questions: Are the sequences P and Q given on separate lines exactly as shown, or can they be split across multiple lines or contain extra whitespace?
Does the i‑th element of P (i.e., P_i) represent the bib number of the person that person i is looking at, or does it represent something else?
Does the i‑th element of Q (i.e., Q_i) represent the bib number of the person wearing bib i, or does it represent the person that bib i is looking at?
Is there any guarantee that the mapping defined by P and Q together forms a valid permutation (i.e., each person is looked at by exactly one other person)?
If a person looks at themselves (i.e., P_i = i or Q_i = i), is that allowed, and how should it be handled?
In case of contradictory information between P and Q (e.g., P_i points to j but Q_j does not point back to i), which array takes precedence for determining S_i?
Should the output be terminated with a newline character after the last number, and are trailing spaces allowed?
What is the required time and memory complexity for the solution, given the constraints up to 3 × 10⁵?

inline_prompts: There are N people numbered from 1 to N. For each i = 1,2,\ldots,N, find the number written on the bib of the person that the person wearing the bib with number i is staring at. Input The input is given from Standard Input in the following format: N P_1 P_2 \dots P_N Q_1 Q_2 \dots Q_N Output Let S_i be the number written on the bib of the person that the person wearing the bib with number i is staring at. Print S_1, S_2, \ldots, S_N in this order, separated by a single space. Constraints - 2 \leq N \leq 3\times 10^5 - 1 \leq P_i \leq N - The values of P_i are distinct. - 1 \leq Q_i \leq N - The values of Q_i are distinct. - All input values are integers.
